<description>
Two test cases (`p2p_v2_encrypted.py` and `p2p_v2_misbehaving.py`) can fail in the -- improbable -- case when network reads happen to arrive in smaller chunks.

Related to #36726 .

All networking code using sockets must not make assumption about the chunking of the incoming/outgoing data, and should be resilient against any chunking. Normally, the chunking of the sends of the writer dictate the chunking of the receives at the reader, but this is not guaranteed by IP/TCP, intermediate networking elements may change the packet structure. In test using sockets on the same host, this is not very likely, but still possible.

Issues:

- `p2p_v2_encrypted.py`:  The v1 message parser in `P2PConnection` rejected the stream as soon as the first 4 bytes did not match the network magic. bitcoind's `V1Transport::readHeader` waits for the full 24-byte header before checking the magic.
The v2 to v1 downgrade relies on bitcoind's behaviour: an outbound v2 connection is only retried with v1 (`V2Transport::ShouldReconnectV1`) if at least a v1 header's worth of bytes had been sent before the peer disconnected. If the node's first send reaches the test peer in small pieces, the Python peer could disconnect after just 4 bytes, the node would not retry with v1, and p2p_v2_encrypted.py would time out waiting for the reconnection.

-  `p2p_v2_misbehaving.py`: Fails for similar root cause. In this test, when the 64-byte key could not be read in one call, the empty array is indexed out-of-bounds, leading to a crash.

The issues were found -- and can be reproduced -- by using a reproducer patch, that forces all socket sends to use smaller chunking. For the run with the reproducer see #36724 .

The issues are test-code only, the non-test code is correct.

The fixes are:

- `p2p_v2_encrypted.py`: Match bitcoind by checking the magic only once the full header has been received.

-  `p2p_v2_misbehaving.py`: Handle the short-read case explicitly, return the data read so far.

These fixes make the test more robust, even though a failure due to this issue in CI is very unlikely, but not impossible.
</description>

- `p2p_v2_misbehaving.py`: guarding the empty `handshake_bytes` return before `random_bitflip(handshake_bytes[:16])` correctly propagates the "not all 64 ellswift bytes received yet" signal instead of bitflipping an empty slice.
